decisions.rationale: The complete NIST entry explicitly names Harter's description. The archived original author page defines dominance trees and then gives its general plan: construct a dominance tree, emit its root, compare the former root's children to establish a new root, and retain losers as children. decisions.limitations: Archived author-defined sorting family, explicitly source-attributed; not independent corroboration or a proof of universal correctness, termination, performance or priority.

decisions.rationale: The NIST entry explicitly links Morin's Java implementation, and his demo index identifies QMSort. Full Java inspection confirms the authored class/comment identity, a random comparison-exchange phase, adjacent comparisons setting change when an inversion exists, and do/while(change) repetition. The candidate carefully describes attempts and control flow rather than claiming that the demonstration always sorts or terminates. The implementation limitations do not contradict that limited procedural description.
decisions.limitations: Original demonstration code, which itself calls this a bad use of randomization. No all-input correctness, termination, practical suitability or performance guarantee is approved; in particular the summary does not promote the source title into such a theorem.

decisions.rationale: NIST names universal B-tree, cites Rudolf Bayer's The Universal B-Tree for multidimensional Indexing, and separately warns of the unlimited-branching homonym. The original VLDB paper's inspected physical PDFp1 identifies Ramsak/Bayer and coauthors, calls its UB-Tree a multidimensional index, and explicitly says it combines B-Tree with Z-curve. Inspected physical PDFp10 maps the cited Bay97 reference to Bayer's universal B-Tree title. These explicit bridges resolve this candidate as the multidimensional universal B-tree, without equating the separate unlimited-branching tree sense.
decisions.limitations: Original research account of the named multidimensional indexing structure. No universal database-performance superiority, complete implementation specification or ambiguous generic UB-tree alias is asserted.
